zh.principle: **标准**：开发网络弹性系统：系统安全工程方法（SP 800-160 第二卷）（Developing Cyber Resilient Systems: A Systems Security Engineering Approach (SP 800-160 Vol.摘要首句把它放进已有文件：「This publication is used in conjunction with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015」，并自陈体裁：「It can be viewed as a handbook for achieving the identified cyber resiliency outcomes based on a systems engineering perspective on system life cycle processes in conjunction with risk management processes, allowing the experience and expertise of the organization to help determine what is correct for its purpose.」§1.1 说明其补位性质：「The purpose of this document is to supplement [SP 800-160 v1] and [SP 800-37]」。关键词行以「risk management strategy; system life cycle; systems security engineering; trustworthiness.」收束主题。四段合起来定体裁与位置：它不自成标准，而是与既有生命周期标准和风险管理框架并用的手册，目的层的取舍交由组织自身经验决定。
zh.why: 风险前提写在卷首综述：「All discussions of cyber resiliency focus on assuring the mission or business functions and are predicated on the assumption that the adversary will breach defenses and establish a long-term presence in organizational systems.」要得到的能力定义为「the ability to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises on systems that use or are enabled by cyber resources」。摘要据此说明组织须自行取舍：「Organizations can select, adapt, and use some or all of the cyber resiliency constructs」。前提与能力并列即是理由：若对手必然进入并长期驻留，只防一次突破并不足以保证任务，弹性构念正是为此列出，且须由组织自行取舍。
zh.used: 该条目用于应用安全工程中的对象定位与步骤复述；引用时先确认输入、参数与版本，再判断结论是否仍适用。
zh.broken: 它自陈不提供步骤手册：卷首使用说明写「It is not intended to provide a specific recipe for execution.」并自比为手册：「it can be viewed as a catalog or handbook for achieving the identified cyber resiliency outcomes」。范围之外另有声明：「Second-order effects are beyond the scope of this publication.」强制力也有限：前言的法定职责段规定「Such information security standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of the appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems.」。最后，这份副本本身已被撤下，见 history 一节。
zh.history: 扉页三行给「NIST Special Publication 800-160」与「Developing Cyber Resilient Systems」，作者行为「RON ROSS VICTORIA PILLITTERI RICHARD GRAUBART DEBORAH BODEAU ROSALIE MCQUAID」；日期行 2019 年 11 月，引用行「Natl.Inst.Stand.Technol.Spec.Publ.800-160, Volume 2, 229 pages (November 2019)」，免费获取行后接 DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-160v2。顶部废止横幅写「The attached publication has been withdrawn (archived), and is provided solely for historical purposes.」并记「SP 800-160 Vol.2 is superseded in its entirety by the publication of SP 800-160 Vol.2 Revision 1.」，取代件为 2021 年 12 月出版的 Vol.2 Revision 1，其 DOI 为 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-160v2r1。致谢页列出评审者，起首一句为「The authors gratefully acknowledge and appreciate the contributions from DJ Anand, Jon Boyens, Nicolas Chaillan, Ed Custeau, Holly Dunlap, Avi Gopstein, Suzanne Hassell, Bill Heinbockel, Daryl Hild, Scott Jackson, Lauren Knausenberger, Ellen Laderman」。扉页、引用行、DOI 与横幅合起来给出这份副本的时间线与地位：2019 年 11 月初版、2021 年 12 月 9 日撤下、由第二卷第 1 修订版整体取代，留存文本仅供历史查阅。

en.principle: **Standard**: Developing Cyber Resilient Systems: A Systems Security Engineering Approach (SP 800-160 Vol. 2) (开发网络弹性系统：系统安全工程方法（SP 800-160 第二卷）). The abstract places the file beside existing ones: "This publication is used in conjunction with ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015" and states its genre: "It can be viewed as a handbook for achieving the identified cyber resiliency outcomes based on a systems engineering perspective on system life cycle processes in conjunction with risk management processes, allowing the experience and expertise of the organization to help determine what is correct for its purpose." Section 1.1 gives its complementary role: "The purpose of this document is to supplement [SP 800-160 v1] and [SP 800-37]". The keyword line closes the subject with "risk management strategy; system life cycle; systems security engineering; trustworthiness."Together the four set the genre and the position: the file is not a standalone standard but a handbook used alongside the life cycle standard and the risk management framework, with the choice among the purpose-level constructs left to the organisation’s own experience.
en.why: The premise sits in the front-matter overview: "All discussions of cyber resiliency focus on assuring the mission or business functions and are predicated on the assumption that the adversary will breach defenses and establish a long-term presence in organizational systems." The property sought is "the ability to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises on systems that use or are enabled by cyber resources", and the abstract draws the consequence for the reader: "Organizations can select, adapt, and use some or all of the cyber resiliency constructs".Premise and property stated side by side are the argument: if the adversary necessarily gets in and stays, defending a single breach does not assure the mission, and the resiliency constructs are listed for exactly that, to be selected and adapted by the organisation.
en.used: Check the input, key or parameters and output format first, then locate the object in its protocol, standard or engineering workflow; do not treat one example parameter set as the only legal set.
en.broken: It declines to be a procedure manual: the front-matter usage note says "It is not intended to provide a specific recipe for execution." and offers itself as "it can be viewed as a catalog or handbook for achieving the identified cyber resiliency outcomes". Part of the subject is excluded outright: "Second-order effects are beyond the scope of this publication." The force is limited too — the authority paragraph states that "Such information security standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of the appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems.". Finally this very copy has been withdrawn, as the history claim records.
en.history: The title block carries "NIST Special Publication 800-160" and "Developing Cyber Resilient Systems", with the author line "RON ROSS VICTORIA PILLITTERI RICHARD GRAUBART DEBORAH BODEAU ROSALIE MCQUAID"; the date line is November 2019, the citation reads "Natl. Inst. Stand. Technol. Spec. Publ. 800-160, Volume 2, 229 pages (November 2019)" and the free-access line is followed by the DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-160v2. The withdrawal banner at the head states "The attached publication has been withdrawn (archived), and is provided solely for historical purposes." and records "SP 800-160 Vol. 2 is superseded in its entirety by the publication of SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Revision 1.", the successor being Volume 2 Revision 1 of December 2021 with the DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-160v2r1. The acknowledgements open with the reviewer list: "The authors gratefully acknowledge and appreciate the contributions from DJ Anand, Jon Boyens, Nicolas Chaillan, Ed Custeau, Holly Dunlap, Avi Gopstein, Suzanne Hassell, Bill Heinbockel, Daryl Hild, Scott Jackson, Lauren Knausenberger, Ellen Laderman".Title block, citation line, DOI and banner give this copy’s timeline and standing together: first published November 2019, withdrawn 9 December 2021, superseded in full by Volume 2 Revision 1, and retained here for historical reference only.

zh: cyber resiliency：预期、承受、恢复并适应借助网络资源的系统所遇不利条件。
construct：本文件对目标、目的、技术、路径与设计原则的合称。
objective：目的层构念，与更高的 goals 分两层。
trustworthiness：值得被信任履行关键要求，含安全、可靠性与 survivability。
system-of-interest：一次弹性工程分析所针对的系统。
tailoring：按组织环境与用例取舍构念与过程。
en: Cyber resiliency: anticipating, withstanding, recovering from and adapting to adverse conditions on systems using cyber resources.
Construct: the umbrella term here for goals, objectives, techniques, approaches and design principles.
Objective: the lower of the two purpose levels, beneath the goals.
Trustworthiness: being worthy of trust to fulfil critical requirements, including resilience and survivability.
System-of-interest: the system a cyber resiliency analysis is carried out on.
Tailoring: selecting and adapting the constructs and processes to the organization’s setting.
